subject: Hot-standby activation procedure & RPO matrix — Beryl Health
messages:
From: Jason Cole <jason.cole@berylhealth.com>

Cc: procurement@berylhealth.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: hot-standby activation procedure + targeted RPOs

Hi Logan / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the architecture looks promising for our regulated workloads. Procurement asked us to collect detailed recovery commitments for the RFP: specifically we need the documented activation procedure for a hot-standby failover and an RPO/RTO matrix mapped to the service tiers we discussed (Production-1, Production-2, Nonprod).

I've attached our standard spreadsheet (Beryl_DR_Template.xlsx) with the columns we expect. Can you: 1) populate the RPO/RTO cells with target values and 2) provide a short runbook excerpt (or activation steps) we can share with our Ops team?

Timing: procurement wants the package by COB Wednesday (2026-11-04).

Questions we have up front:
- Do you support automated prefix KV warm-cache transfer as part of activation?
- Can you guarantee cross-region KV sync to meet the RPO you populate?
- What are the manual escalation points and expected operator roles during activation?

Appreciate a concise response (table + short bulleted activation steps).

Best,
Jason Cole
Senior Infrastructure Architect
Beryl Health

[attachment: Beryl_DR_Template.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Request: hot-standby activation procedure + targeted RPOs

Jason — thanks for the clear asks and the template. We'll fill the spreadsheet and include a concise activation excerpt. High level summary up front to help procurement:

- Target RPO (prod-1): 60s for session-level state, 5m for full KV sync; RTO: 3m to route-level failover, 15m to achieve steady-state throughput.
- Target RPO (prod-2): 5m RPO, RTO 30m.
- Nonprod: 1h RPO, RTO 2h.

Short answers to your bullets:
- Prefix/KV warm-cache transfer: supported via automatic KV snapshot + streaming diff during cutover for models with compatible key schemas. For very low RPOs we rely on continuous replication (see attached runbook excerpt).
- Cross-region KV sync: we support asynchronous replication by default; for sub-2m RPOs we recommend hybrid approach (continuous replication + short-lived transactional mirroring during cutover) — we describe the operator steps in the runbook.
- Escalation & roles: primary on-call (customer-facing SRE), Redwood on-call engineer, and Platform Ops lead (listed in runbook): operator triggers automated route flip, monitors token-level backlog, and escalates to DRI if post-cutover error rate >2%.

Next steps:
1) Monica will populate the spreadsheet with the explicit numbers and attach a minimal runbook excerpt (activation-diagram-v2.png).
2) Ben will follow up on commercial language for the RTO/RPO commitments for the SOW.
3) Propose a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the cutover sequence — are you available 10:00-10:30 PT?

Ill attach the filled template when Monica confirms.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Director, Platform Solutions
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: hot-standby activation procedure + targeted RPOs

Jason — attaching the populated spreadsheet and a short activation excerpt. See key items below and the runbook snippet embedded.

Attachments: Beryl_DR_Template.xlsx (populated), activation-diagram-v2.png

Activation excerpt (summary):
1) Pre-check (T minus 60m): verify cross-region replication health (replication lag < 30s for prod-1), token queue < 2k, and warm-cache hit rate > 75%. Run: ./ops/replication-health --region us-west || abort
2) Prepare target region: ensure model artifacts pinned to vX.Y.Z and quantization profile loaded. Allocate hot-standby pool (autoscaler: reserve 1.2x baseline tokens/s for 15m burst).
3) Snapshot + streaming diff: take KV snapshot and begin streaming diffs. For prod-1 we recommend a final 60s grace window where write forwarding is enabled to both regions to capture late writes.
4) DNS/edge cutover (T plus 0m): update smart-routing policy to prefer target region; soft-failover requests remain on origin for fallback for 2m.
5) Validation (T plus 2-15m): run canary traffic at 5-10% ramp, validate latency P50/P95 within targets, verify token consumption and cost telemetry.
6) Roll forward (T plus 15-60m): increase traffic to 100% once validation gates pass; monitor for 30m. If error budget exceeded (>2% 5m error rate) trigger rollback to origin and open urgent incident.

RPO/RTO matrix (populated from template):
- Production-1: RPO = 60 seconds (session-level), RTO = 3 minutes (route-level), full steady-state recovery = 15 minutes.
- Production-2: RPO = 5 minutes, RTO = 30 minutes.
- Nonprod: RPO = 1 hour, RTO = 2 hours.

Notes and caveats:
- Very low RPOs (sub-60s) require customer acceptance of increased cross-region replication costs and may require per-customer tuning of KV sharding.
- For models using very large KV caches, warm-cache time can exceed the stated RTO; in those cases we rely on prefix caching and progressive ramp.
- We document exact operator commands (ops-runbook section 4.2) in the enclosed runbook excerpt.

Requested deliverables: we included the populated Beryl_DR_Template.xlsx with the numeric commitments and a two-page runbook excerpt (embedded in the email body below for quick review). Let us know if you want the full runbook as a secured Drive link.

Runbook snippet (excerpt):
---
Operator command checklist (activation):
- runbook verify-replication --region origin,target
- reserve-hot-pool --cluster target --multiplier 1.2
- kv-snapshot --prefix all --output /tmp/bryl-snap-$(date +%s)
- start-stream-diff --from-snap /tmp/bryl-snap-*
---

If this looks good we'll join procurement's bundle tomorrow. Also confirming the 10:00 PT slot is open for a 30-minute walkthrough.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
